note: PDS rerun recipes. ONE recipe per ledger row (two recipes sharing a subject and a null quantity are two rival claims on one conflict key, and grip would flag both CONFLICT). Every `terms` value must occur LITERALLY in both `command` and `claim` — that binding is what makes a claim falsifiable: mutate the claim, keep the command byte-identical, and the harness reds. A recipe re-derives ONE bound sub-claim of its row, never the row's whole reason; the verdict line says so, and says nothing stronger.

recipes.claim: The PDS harness file the row's whole cost argument rests on — scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh — is still present in origin/main.
recipes.binds: The row's reason cites pds-pull-proof.sh:2546. This recipe re-derives the FILE's existence at a named ref, which is all `git cat-file` moves its exit code on; the cited LINE is not re-derived here and must not be read as though it were. `-t` rather than `-e` on purpose: both are polarised (0 present / 128 absent) and grip's screen admits both, but `-e` prints nothing and grip's classifySilence rules a silent success NULL-READ, so the honest predicate arrives saying nothing. `-t` prints `blob` and survives.

recipes.claim: The token hzResDone still occurs under internal/cli in origin/main, so the row's subject has not been renamed or deleted out from under it.
recipes.binds: The row asserts a 50-call-site population. This recipe re-derives only that the TOKEN is still there — the count is a separate claim and is deliberately NOT asserted here, because `git grep -n` moves its exit code on presence, not on cardinality.

recipes.claim: The commit 6e53d27824206c5cbda4eb8916795921064165e9 that this row's reason re-derived itself against is an ancestor of origin/main, so the reason was written against history this branch still contains.
recipes.binds: `git branch --contains` and `git rev-list --count <sha>..origin/main` both exit 0 for an ancestor AND a non-ancestor, so neither can ever red; the direction here (origin/main..<sha>, graded by grep) was measured polarised on this host. `grep -x` rather than `grep -qx`: -q suppresses the match, and grip's classifySilence rules a matcher that exits 0 without printing a NULL-READ, so the -q spelling is polarised at the shell and mute at the verdict layer.

recipes.claim: internal/cli/export_cmd.go still carries no completeness signal in origin/main — the token completeness does not occur in it.
recipes.binds: This command exits 1. That is the whole point of PDS-D389: the exit code is nonzero BECAUSE the claim is an absence and the absence holds. It is ruled through grip's shipped admitsAbsenceClaim, never through `verdict == ADMITTED`, which would call this true reason false.

recipes.claim: scripts/go-literal-check.sh --selftest exits 1 on a healthy gate on macOS.
recipes.binds: SHIPPED AS A KNOWN REFUSAL, ON PURPOSE. grip's caller-boundary screen refuses every script runner (bash/sh/zsh/node) because they execute arbitrary programs, so this reason CANNOT be re-derived by this instrument today and is reported REFUSED with that named reason. It is here rather than absent because a class of reason that can only be checked by RUNNING something is exactly the class this wave was told to make visible and bounded rather than to pretend is checkable.
